newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy may need 25 trln lire EMU mini-budget -- BCI.
newsitem.headline: Italy may need 25 trln lire EMU mini-budget -- BCI.

text.p: Italy may need an extra 25 trillion lire "mini-budget" to reduce its deficit/GDP ratio to the 3.0 percent level for early entry into European economic and monetary union, Banca Commerciale Italiana (BCI) said.

BCI's research office said in a market note that the government's nominal 62.5 trillion lire 1997 draft budget might only raise a real 50 trillion lire, resulting in a public administration deficit/GDP ratio of 4.3 percent next year.
To reach the 3.0 percent EMU target, extra deficit-cutting measures of 25 trillion lire would therefore be needed, it said.

BCI forecast the public administration deficit at 7.3 percent of gross domestic product this year and revised upwards its estimate for the 1996 PSBR to 137 trillion lire. The latest government estimate is for a year-end deficit of 130 trillion.
"The poor state of public finances both in 1996 and in 1997 has not yet been completely incorporated in (bond) market prices," BCI said.
